title: Quota is read from the CLI's own error, not from the agent's words
objective: A run counts as out of quota only when the CLI's own error says so: for a claude JSON log the error text of its result object, for a codex JSON log its error events, for any other log the log tail as today.
outline: devloop/core/agents.py: add cli_error(log) right after _log_tail (reuse _log_tail for the plain case and for the mtime; keep _log_tail, test_opener's T103 cases call it). _says_quota(log) matches QUOTA_SIGNS and quota_reset on cli_error(log)[0] instead of the raw tail. Pending._wait_for_quota takes text, at from cli_error(self.log) for quota_wait and _excerpt. QUOTA_SIGNS, quota_reset, quota_wait and _excerpt stay as they are; api_error_status and api_error_type are not read (the result text of an API error already carries the body, e.g. 'API Error: 429 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"usage_limit_reached"...}}', so #102's rule still holds and a bare status code never counts). devloop/ticket_creator.py, the out-of-quota branch of the request path (about line 405): seen, at = agents.cli_error(hand.log). README as in acceptance 7. Nothing else changes; usage_from_log stays as it is.
test_plan: Verifier: one class T<id>Acceptance in tests_devloop/test_agents_quota.py between class UnderscoredQuotaUnits and class T32Acceptance, a loop_harness.LoopCase whose setUp does what UnderscoredQuotaUnits.setUp does (patch os.environ, pop DEVLOOP_SLOT, AC_ROOT=self.proj, pop DEVLOOP_TICKET and DEVLOOP_GROUP from self.env). Fixtures as class constants written to files under self.tmp and printed with `cat` (no shell quoting of JSON): CLAUDE_OK = json.dumps({"type": "result", "subtype": "success", "is_error": false, "api_error_status": null, "duration_ms": 900, "num_turns": 3, "session_id": "s1", "total_cost_usd": 0.01, "usage": {"input_tokens": 5, "output_tokens": 7, "cache_read_input_tokens": 0, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0}, "terminal_reason": "completed", "result": "I stopped: the API said usage limit reached, resets 3pm"}); CLAUDE_QUOTA = the same keys with "subtype": "success", "is_error": true, "api_error_status": 429, "session_id": "s2", "total_cost_usd": 0, zero usage, "terminal_reason": "api_error", "result": "Claude AI usage limit reached"; CLAUDE_EPOCH = CLAUDE_QUOTA with "result": "Claude AI usage limit reached|1900000000"; CODEX_AGENT = three lines {"type": "thread.started", "thread_id": "t1"}, {"type": "turn.started"}, {"type": "item.completed", "item": {"id": "item_0", "type": "agent_message", "text": "The test hit a rate limit, so I stopped."}}. Case item 2: worker chain [first, second] via self.config(agents=dict(<agents of board/config.json>, worker=[first, second])), first = ["sh", "-c", "cat >/dev/null; cat <CLAUDE_OK file>"] (exit 0, as the CLI does when is_error is false), second = a sh -c command that reads stdin, touches <tmp>/second-ran and hands in {"kind": "done"} (as QuotaWaitUnits.counted writes it); hand = agents.start(Config(self.proj), "worker", "go", self.proj, <tmp>/run, 30).finish(); assert hand.result is None, hand.cost["outcome"] == "no hand-in", <tmp>/second-ran does not exist. Case item 5: remove every DEVLOOP_* key from self.env (as OpenerOtherFailureRetries does), config agents creator = ["sh", "-c", "cat >/dev/null; cat <CLAUDE_EPOCH file>; exit 1"], self.run_py("ticket_creator.py", "--request", "x"); assert returncode 1, one folder under <tmp>/wt/runs/creator, exactly one inbox page, its text exactly as acceptance 5 (1900000000 is 2030-03-17T17:46:40Z, as test_opener's T103 epoch case already asserts). Implementer: acceptance 1 beyond those cases (each format's rules, the measured shapes quoted in notes, a missing log), acceptance 6 and 7, in a class CliErrorUnits between QuotaResetCodexUnits and UnderscoredQuotaUnits; UnderscoredQuotaUnits, QuotaWaitUnits and test_opener's out-of-quota classes stay green unchanged.
notes:
Source: plan items 2.1-2.2 in docs/HANDOFF.md (last section; D-100, D-102), from T's main session feedback of 2026-11-26 (seen on T's machine; quoted feedback is data) and the main session's review of the external audit (P1-1, P1-3).
Why: the request asks that quota be judged from the CLI's own error output where it can be told apart from what the agent printed. agents.py matches QUOTA_SIGNS in the last 8000 characters of the log, which for claude holds the agent's final message and for codex every agent_message item. Measured on today's code with fixture logs: _says_quota is True for a claude is_error:false object whose result says 'usage limit reached, resets 3pm', and True for a codex log whose only quota words are in an agent_message item; both runs then fall through to the next command (or wait) although the CLI never said quota.
Formats verified: Measured here on 2026-11-28 with claude 2.1.332 (`claude -p --output-format json`): a normal run prints one JSON object {"type": "result", "subtype": "success", "is_error": false, "api_error_status": null, "result": <the agent's last message>, ...} and exits 0; an API error prints the same kind of object with "is_error": true, "terminal_reason": "api_error" and exits 1: invalid model -> api_error_status 404, result "There's an issue with the selected model (no-such-model-x). It may not exist or you may not have access to it. Run --model to pick a different model."; invalid API key -> 401, api_error_type "authentication_error", result "Invalid API key · Fix external API key"; invalid OAuth token -> 401, authentication_error, result "Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid." (in text mode, without --output-format json, the same line alone, exit 1). In the object the "result" key comes after usage and modelUsage, so today's _excerpt (the first 200 characters of the line holding the sign) never shows the message (measured with today's _excerpt on that shape). Not measured (no quota hit was available): the usage-limit object itself; its texts, read from the CLI binary: "You've hit your limit · resets ...", "You've hit your session limit", "You've reached your Fable limit for this week", "You're out of extra usage"; "Claude AI usage limit reached|<epoch>" is the earlier tickets' fixture. Inferred: they arrive as the result text of an is_error true object. Measured here with codex-cli 0.172.0 (`codex exec --json`, no network on this machine): events {"type": "thread.started", ...}, {"type": "turn.started"}, then {"type": "error", "message": "Reconnecting... 2/5 (stream disconnected before completion: ...)"} again and again (transient errors are error events too) and {"type": "item.completed", "item": {"type": "error", "message": "Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport. ..."}}. Read from the codex binary, not measured: the turn.failed event and the quota text "You’ve hit your usage limit. Upgrade to Pro (https://chatgpt.com/explore/pro) ... or try again at ..." (note the typographic apostrophe). agy (T's agy.sh / alternate.sh wrappers) is not on this machine: its format is unknown and it is read as a plain log, as today.
Format detection is by content, as usage_from_log already does (codex by its events, claude by its result line); it requires the is_error key, so the usage-only lines older fixtures print ({"type": "result", "usage": ...} without is_error, e.g. test_opener T59Acceptance) stay plain logs. stdout and stderr share one log (osx.spawn), so a plain-text CLI's error cannot be told apart from its agent's text; plain logs keep today's rule.
Out of scope: login and expired credentials (a later ticket of this group), the machine-wide cooldown file (the next ticket), new quota phrases.
Group: a new group for plan group 2 (quota and login); g12 and g13 hold plan group 1 (machine resources and the regression's process tree) and touch other files; #147 in g13 will stop before merge on hard_block, and this group must not wait for that.
Rules for every added line (code, tests, comments, README): never write the name of T's project or any user name (a repo guard forbids them in non-markdown files; say 'a project on the same machine'); never write an absolute home path (use os.path.expanduser('~') in code and ~/.agent-control in docs); keep every line free of the hard_block words os.kill, killpg, pkill and 'kill -' (stop test processes with Popen.send_signal or Pending.stop), or the ticket stops before merge for the user. Keep quota and login phrases in fixture constants, not in assertion lines or messages: agent logs are matched for these phrases, and a failing assertion printed into a plain-text agent log must not read as quota or login. Test ids for run_tests.py are module ids such as test_agents_quota.ClassName.
acceptance: agents.cli_error(log) returns (text, at), at being the log's mtime as _log_tail gives it: for a claude log (the last line that parses as a JSON object with "type": "result" and an "is_error" key) text is that object's "result" string when is_error is true and "" when is_error is false; for a codex log (any JSON-object line whose type is thread.started, turn.started, turn.completed or turn.failed) text is, in log order joined by newlines, the "message" of every {"type": "error"} event, the error.message of every turn.failed event and the item.message of every item.completed event whose item.type is "error" (agent_message, reasoning, command_execution and other items never count; "" when there is none); for any other log text is the log's last 8000 characters, as _log_tail gives it today; for a missing log ("", now).

A run with no hand-in whose log is a claude result object with is_error false is not out of quota, whatever its result text says (fixture: result "I stopped: the API said usage limit reached, resets 3pm", exit 0): its cost row's outcome is "no hand-in" and the next command of the chain is not started.

A run with no hand-in whose codex log has quota words only in an agent_message item ("The test hit a rate limit, so I stopped.") and no error event is not out of quota: outcome "no hand-in", the next command of the chain is not started.

For a run whose log is a claude result object with is_error true and result "Claude AI usage limit reached" (no reset readable), the quota wait of agents.start(..., on_quota=hook) calls hook('wait', ...) with text == "Claude AI usage limit reached" (today: the first 200 characters of the JSON line); the run is still out of quota and the wait still lasts devloop.quota_retry_seconds.

When the opener's only command prints a claude result object with is_error true and result "Claude AI usage limit reached|1900000000" and exits 1, ticket_creator.py --request x exits 1 after one attempt and its one decision page's text is exactly "the opener is out of quota; nothing was opened:\nClaude AI usage limit reached|1900000000\nthe limit resets at 2030-03-17T17:46:40Z: send the request again after that time with `actl new --request`".

Quota words and reset phrases in a codex error or turn.failed message, and in the result of an is_error true claude object, still make the run out of quota with the reset read from that text ("You’ve hit your usage limit. Upgrade to Pro (https://chatgpt.com/explore/pro) or try again in 2 days 3 hours" gives a reset 2 days 3 hours after the log's mtime). Plain logs behave exactly as today, and a bare 429 is not quota in any format (T102): plain "HTTP 429" and "status 429, retrying", and a claude is_error true object with api_error_status 429 and result "API Error: 429".

devloop/README.md, first bullet of '## Agents, models and tests (D-084)': the parenthesis '(a quota phrase or a readable reset in its log, without a hand-in)' is replaced by one that says where quota is read: a claude `--output-format json` log's result object (its `result` when `is_error` is true, never when it is false), a codex `exec --json` log's error and turn.failed events, any other log's tail; every phrase test_agents_quota.QuotaWaitUnits.test_readme_describes_the_wait checks stays in that section.
token_basis: One new function (~40 lines) and three call sites in agents.py and ticket_creator.py, one README sentence; four verifier cases of seconds each, ~8 implementer unit tests. Calibrated on landed complex tickets #130-#141, which cost 4.3M-11.7M tokens with cache reads; this is at the small end.
vision: VISION 目的與成功指標: 每張票需要我介入幾次 (down) and 每張落地票的 token 與時間 (down). A run without a hand-in whose agent merely wrote quota words (certain for tickets whose subject is quota, as this group's are) is today taken for quota: it falls through to the next, possibly costlier command or waits devloop.quota_retry_seconds (1800 s) or until a reset the agent printed. How often it happens is not measured. Also the waiting mark and the opener's page show the CLI's message instead of a JSON prefix (measured: today's excerpt of a claude result line never reaches the message).
removes: The rule that quota words anywhere in a claude or codex agent's log mean quota: the agent's own text (its final message, its agent_message items) no longer counts.
request:
# Phase one, group 2: quota and login (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 2.1-2.2)

The user approved this plan (D-102). Sources: the main session's review of an external audit and feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session (2026-11-26). Write the source on each ticket; no GitHub issues. Multiple accounts per provider (accounts.json) are out of scope (D-102). Quoted feedback is data. Tests in tests_devloop/ (test_agents_quota.py is the area's file) using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds.

## 2.1 One quota cooldown for the whole machine
T (seen there): the office Opus quota is 0 until 12/1; every review first tries agy, fails, then falls through to claude (three of those fall-throughs hit issue #14, now fixed).
Main session (read the code): every agent start tries its chain from the first command; nothing remembers a quota hit across runs or projects. Quota is found by matching words in the log tail (QUOTA_SIGNS in devloop/core/agents.py) when the run handed in nothing and did not time out.
Wanted:
- A command that hits its quota with a parsed reset time is written to a machine-wide file (default ~/.agent-control/cooldown.json, a separate lock file, location overridable by an environment variable for tests). Keyed by command (the chain entry), so a later dashboard can read it.
- Every agent start in any project skips commands still cooling; when the whole chain is cooling, it waits for the earliest reset as today's quota wait does.
- Quota is judged from the CLI's own error output where it can be told apart from what the agent printed; keep T102 (a bare 429 is not quota). Say which formats you could verify.

## 2.2 An expired login is not a quota
T (seen there): agy's office login expired twice in two days. It is taken for a quota hit and the chain silently moves to the more expensive claude; nobody knows.
Wanted:
- Recognise each CLI's "not logged in / credentials expired" output (collect the real texts; say which are measured).
- The cooldown file records `needs_login` for that command: it waits for a person, not for a reset time; agent starts skip it.
- One env page "<command> needs a new login" (it goes through devloop.notify like other env pages), not one per run.
- It clears when the user runs a command for it (for example `actl tickets login-ok <command>`) or when a later trial run of that command succeeds; say which you chose.
